subject: AtlasAI private GPU sizing and egress/surge mapping
messages:
From: Lena Zhou <lena@atlasai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Sizing for private GPU deployment — AtlasAI burst scenario

Sergio / team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We ran a short spike against our staging VPC and attached a small sample of the burst trace (atlas_traffic_sample.csv). The key asks:

- We need guidance on a private GPU pool that can sustain our 99th percentile burst profile (short spikes up to ~3.2k concurrent requests for ~2–5 minutes), while keeping steady-state cost below our committed budget.
- Important hard constraints: all inference traffic must stay inside our VPC (no egress to public Redwood-hosted endpoints), and we need KV-cache warmup to succeed within 30s when a pool scales up.
- We'd like recommended throughput targets (qps, tokens/sec) per GPU type, a proposed warm-pool size, and an egress/bandwidth budget for peering.

Can you send a short sizing sketch and a proposed MW (mutual action plan) we can review with infra?

Attachments: atlas_traffic_sample.csv (csv, 750KB)

Thanks,
Lena Zhou
Head of Platform
AtlasAI

---
Lena Zhou
AtlasAI

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Zhou <lena@atlasai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Sizing for private GPU deployment — AtlasAI burst scenario

Hi Lena — thanks for the trace, that’s helpful. High level thoughts after a quick pass:

- Short answer: we can meet the burst envelope with a combination of reserved warm-pool + on-demand burst slabs. My team will produce a numeric sketch, but expect a warm-pool sized for ~20% of observed peak to keep tail latency low while autoscale populates the rest.
- Network: given the VPC-only constraint, peering bandwidth needs headroom for both model KV cache transfers and active token egress. For your traffic shape I estimate ~6–8 Gbps sustained per 1k concurrent token-generation QPS at median seq lengths — we’ll refine.
- KV-cache warmup: we’ll recommend pre-warming policies and a small shared prefix cache for the warm-pool to reduce cold-start token costs; that will be part of the attachment.

I’ve attached an initial capacity worksheet (sergio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with rough slot math and two GPU shape options (A100/q4_0 and 80GB-similar quantized). Karthik, can you review the kernel/runtime assumptions and add network egress math? Marissa — once we align on numbers I’ll draft an action plan for Atlas infra + our deployment handoff.

Next steps I propose: quick sync with Atlas infra (30m) to validate peering + firewall constraints, then a follow-up with MC to finalize the SLA carveouts.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sergio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

Thanks, Sergio. I pulled the trace and ran a quick back-of-envelope using Redwood runtime profiles. Key technical inputs / assumptions I used (see kv-cache-warmup-notes.md attached):

- Model profile: 2048 context, typical prompt+response length median 120 tokens, p95 420 tokens
- A100-80GB quantized throughput (in our runtime) ~350 tokens/sec per GPU for the p95 mix; 80GB-class compressed runs ~1.8x throughput for short sequences — I used conservative 1.4x to account for network and overheads
- Warm-pool behavior: we recommend pre-warm occupancy at 20–25% of observed peak concurrent requests to keep admission latency below 120ms for p50 and sub-2s for p99 during initial phase while autoscale adds slabs
- Egress math: pulled from sergio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx — for your trace I estimate peak egress of ~9 Gbps for 3.2k concurrent at p95 token rates (includes model shard fetch + active token streaming). This assumes 1.2x multiplier for TLS + framing overheads.

Sizing suggestion (very high level):
- Steady-state commit: 40 GPUs (A100-equivalent) for baseline sustained QPS and cost predictability
- Warm-pool: 8 GPUs (20% of peak) always warm in your VPC; these have shared prefix cache pinned
- Burst slabs: on-demand slabs to add another ~32 GPUs when scaling to the 3.2k concurrent peak (target populate in <= 90s with pre-warm policy)
- Network: provision 25 Gbps peering with autoscaling headroom to 40 Gbps for short bursts; add NAT + flow logs for audit (you requested).

Caveats: these numbers are conservative for p95/p99. If Atlas is willing to accept a slightly higher p99 during extreme spikes we can reduce warm-pool size and save on commit cost. I put some of the math into an attachment.

Attachment: kv-cache-warmup-notes.md (md, 8KB)

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Sizing for private GPU deployment — AtlasAI burst scenario (Mutual Action Plan + next steps)

Lena / team — summary and agreed MW below. I copied Atlas infra and added links to a shared drive folder where we'll keep final artifacts.

Summary decisions (agreed):
- Commit: Atlas will procure a baseline of 40 A100-equivalent GPUs in the VPC (reserved) for predictability.
- Warm-pool: 8 GPUs pinned as warm (20% of observed peak). Warm-pool will run shared prefix KV cache with pre-warm script executed during maintenance windows.
- Burst slabs: Redwood to enable autoscale slabs up to +32 GPUs; target populate time <= 90s with pre-warm; fallback model variant (lower memory, higher latency) allowed after 180s.
- Network: Atlas to provision initial peering at 25 Gbps with autoscale alerts to upgrade to 40 Gbps during sustained bursts >3 minutes. NAT + flow logs required for audit.

Mutual Action Plan (owner / ETA):
1) Atlas infra: confirm peering CIDR and firewall allowlist (owner: Atlas infra; ETA: 2026-10-12)
2) Redwood (Sergio): provide final capacity worksheet and per-GPU throughput table (owner: Sergio; ETA: 2026-10-09) — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2BAtlasAI-privdeploy
3) Redwood (Karthik): finalize KV-cache warmup script + warm-pool pre-warm plan (owner: Karthik; ETA: 2026-10-11)
4) Atlas + Redwood: run a staged spike test (30m) during a maintenance window to validate populate times and p99 latency (ETA: week of 2026-10-18)

Attachments I uploaded to the shared folder: privdeploy-map.drawio (network topology), sergio_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (capacity math), kv-cache-warmup-notes.md

Questions / open items:
- Is Atlas comfortable with the fallback model variant at 180s? If not we need a larger warm-pool and higher commit.
- Do you want flow logs shipped to Redwood audit S3 bucket or kept within Atlas for first 90 days?

If that looks good I'll convert this into a short SOW and a HubSpot deal update (DEAL-8473).

Thanks — MC
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: privdeploy-map.drawio (drawio, 45KB)
